title: Terawww (Teraw) — Indie Game Developer · WriteNor
description: Terawww, also known as Teraw and Терав, is an independent game developer and the creator of WriteNor, a first-person psychological horror. Official portfolio.
avatar: Terawww — Independent game developer, creator of WriteNor
sub: I’m Terawww. I make psychological horror games about memory, perception and the things we leave unresolved. Creator of WriteNor.
aboutblocks: Terawww is my developer name. You may also know me as Teraw, Терав or Тераввв. This is my official portfolio: the place to find my game, its current status and my public links.
I develop independent psychological horror games. My current project is WriteNor: a first-person story in which a frozen present meets memories that keep moving forward.
The detail you almost miss. A familiar room that feels different. A conversation that means something else when you remember it later. I want curiosity and unease to carry the player into the story.
skills: Spaces, light and pacing that make an ordinary place feel unfamiliar.
Environmental details that reward attention and invite questions.
Messages, screens and files as part of the player’s investigation.
Memories, dialogue and small discoveries that change how a scene feels.
A creative focus on the gap between what happened and what someone remembers.
Silence, distance and rhythm as part of a scene’s atmosphere.
logline: “A day that will not end. A past that will not stay buried.”
gamedesc: WriteNor is a first-person psychological horror. Johnny’s present stands still while memories take him back a year, to the office and to Nori. Explore, read messages and piece together why those two realities are drawing closer. Some truths only surface when you are willing to remember.
archive: The Last Command is an early prototype of the future game WriteNor by Terawww. It is available for Windows and Linux on itch.io. Its first beta was published in August 2025.
philosophy: A familiar place, one wrong detail
A scene can be unsettling before anything happens. Small changes give the player a reason to look again.
I want the player to keep going because they need to understand the place, the people and the memory behind it.
A room, a message or a pause in a conversation can carry a story. I prefer details the player finds to answers delivered all at once.
Horror stays with us when there is something human underneath it. Memory, absence and unfinished conversations are at the heart of WriteNor.
quote: “Make the player want to remember — even when it hurts.”
